title: Just 25% of Americans Plan to Dress Up for Halloween
paragraphs: Halloween is one of the most popular holidays in the US. But according to a new survey, most Americans are not planning to wear a costume this year.

The survey was carried out by Talker Research, which asked 2,000 Americans about their Halloween plans between September 2 and September 8, 2026. It found that 76% of people were not planning to dress up for Halloween. In other words, fewer than one in four Americans planned to wear a costume.
Many people also seem to be skipping Halloween parties. According to the survey, 77% said they had no plans to go to a Halloween party this year.
Younger people were more interested in dressing up. According to the survey, Gen Z and millennial respondents were about 10% more likely to wear a costume than people from older generations.

The survey also asked people which costumes they think are "played out," meaning they have been used too often and are no longer interesting. The top answer was the "sexy" version of any costume, chosen by 29% of people. This was followed by pirates at 25%, the Joker at 22%, cowboys and cowgirls at 21%, and Harley Quinn at 18%. Some people, however, said they were planning very unusual costumes, such as a circus peanut candy or a Polish sausage.
Even though most people are not dressing up themselves, many still think costumes are for everyone. About 68% agreed that no one is ever too old to dress up for Halloween.
Other recent surveys have found similar results. A poll by Ipsos found that 26% of Americans dress up in a costume during the Halloween season.
Halloween is celebrated every year on October 31. Even if fewer adults are wearing costumes, many people still enjoy other traditions, such as giving out candy to children who go trick-or-treating.
